description: Team IGNISPHERE (Cairo/Giza) builds FlameMargin: an AI fire-safety margin tool for spacecraft cabins trained on NASA's BASS-II ISS fire experiments. It predicts whether a material keeps burning, with uncertainty, flags conditions outside NASA's data (like the Artemis 8.2 psia / 34% O2 atmosphere), and explains results through a grounded AI Copilot. Skills: machine learning, data analysis, combustion science, web apps and AI agents. Live: flamemargin.streamlit.app
summary:
FlameMargin is an AI fire-safety margin tool for spacecraft cabins, built on NASA's own ISS fire experiments (BASS-II, NASA/TM-20210011385). NASA screens flight materials with a test run in Earth gravity, yet BASS-II showed that materials can burn at lower oxygen in microgravity. The Artemis Exploration Atmosphere (8.2 psia / 34% O2) is also richer than the ISS cabin and above the 31.4% O2 limit with no burning-rate increase.

For a material, oxygen level and airflow, FlameMargin answers three questions: Will it burn? How sure are we? Is this condition even inside NASA's data? It has three layers: a Prediction Engine (P(burn) with 90% intervals for five materials, trained on 192 labelled points from 85 tests and validated leave-one-test-out: AUC 0.82, Brier skill +26%), an interactive Flammability Map and Mission Board (ISS, Artemis, lunar habitat), and a Fire Safety Copilot that answers only with the model's numbers and cites the NASA tests behind each answer.

Key finding: none of NASA's 126 BASS-II tests comes close to the Artemis cabin, so FlameMargin flags it as out of distribution instead of guessing, showing where margins are thin and where the next experiment is needed.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

1) Prediction Engine: for a material, O2 %, forced-flow speed and thickness, it returns P(burn) (the probability that a flame survives) with a 90% bootstrap interval, plus the three nearest real NASA tests (test ID, the crew's own words and the report page). Five materials: SIBAL fabric, PMMA film, PMMA slab, PMMA rod and Nomex; flame spread rate for PMMA slabs. An out-of-distribution (OOD) guard (material, pressure, gravity, configuration and tested O2 / flow / size ranges, plus a nearest-neighbour distance check) stops the model from giving a number where NASA has no data.

2) Flammability Map and Mission Board: P(burn) over O2 x airflow with the 0.5 boundary, uncertainty band, every NASA test plotted, a 3D view and a 'Margin' gauge (O2 distance to the predicted extinction line). The Mission Board shows ISS cabin, Artemis Exploration Atmosphere and a lunar habitat against all five materials; outside NASA's data a tile says NO DATA instead of guessing. An Evidence Gap view plots all 126 BASS-II tests against these mission atmospheres.

3) Fire Safety Copilot: an AI agent (English and Arabic) that answers only through the model's tools. Code checks every number and NASA test ID against the tool results, puts OOD warnings first and falls back to a deterministic mode if the LLM fails.

HOW WE BUILT AND VALIDATED IT

We transcribed all 126 BASS-II tests from the report (Appendix A Tables A.1-A.6, Tables 7.1 and 5.1) and labelled burn vs extinguished with written rules; every point keeps a verbatim quote and page. Result: 192 points from 85 tests (166 burn, 26 extinguished). Cross-checks: 31/31 SIBAL rows match Zhao et al. (2015); an independent re-extraction of 20% of rows matched 26/26. We compared logistic regression, a Gaussian process and gradient boosting with leave-one-test-out validation. The shipped model scores AUC 0.82 and Brier 0.087 vs 0.118 for a no-skill baseline (+26% skill), and misses 1 of 166 NASA burns at the 0.5 line. A pre-registered v2.1 lost on Brier, so we did not ship it. Copilot: 14/15 adversarial evaluation questions passed; 334 automated tests pass.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Fast, transparent screening of cabin materials and airflow with the NASA evidence behind each answer, and a clear map of where NASA's microgravity fire data ends (for example the Artemis atmosphere), pointing to the experiments that are still needed. It is decision support, not a replacement for NASA-STD-6001 testing.

CREATIVITY AND FACTORS CONSIDERED

Instead of a model that always gives an answer, FlameMargin is built to know where its knowledge ends: honesty about uncertainty and data coverage is a feature, not a footnote. Limits: data are at about 1 atm and in microgravity only, for five materials. Next: tests at 8.2 psia / 34% O2 as they are published, FM2 lunar-gravity data and Saffire large-scale fire data.

TOOLS

Python, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, pdfplumber, Plotly, Streamlit (Streamlit Community Cloud), Google Gemini via the google-genai SDK with function calling, PyYAML, pytest, GitHub.

Code (MIT): https://github.com/badr5556/FlameMargin
